title: Cambridge fair housing source-of-income protection
requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not refuse to rent or discriminate in housing transactions because of an applicant's source of income, including Section 8 and public benefits.
key_value: source of income protected, includes Section 8
coverage_conditions: Real estate transactions in Cambridge, including viewing or renting an apartment and the terms and conditions of tenancy.
exemptions: Two-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
penalty: Civil fines up to $300 for each violation; the Commission may also seek damages, expenses and injunctive relief.
citation: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, ch. 14.04: source of income
quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits

note: Ordinance only requires giving tenants a rights and resources guide; it sets no rent, eviction, deposit or screening rule.

title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260
requirement: The Office of Landlord Tenant Relations administers and enforces the Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance regulating rents on covered properties; owners may apply for a permitted exemption.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Jersey City subject to rent control; all 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control.
exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control; other permitted exemptions are granted on application to the Office.
quoted_span: Just type in the Property Address, Confirm the Property Location, and select “Property Rent Control Status” under “Request Category.” Be sure to provide your phone number and email address so that the staff can sufficiently fulfill this request. (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)

title: LA motion to study a ban on algorithmic rent-setting
requirement: The Council would instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to report how many owners and managers use algorithm-based software to set rents and whether a ban is feasible.
coverage_conditions: Ownership and management entities using algorithm-based software to establish rents in the City of Los Angeles.

applicability.other: entities using algorithm-based software to set rents

citation: Los Angeles City Council Motion 24-1031: algorithmic rent setting, study and possible ban
quoted_span:
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set
rents in the City.
interaction: Would instruct a study of a city ban; the packet notes San Francisco approved such a ban in July 2024.

title: LA Just Cause Ordinance: just cause and relocation assistance
requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered tenancy without just cause, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions; at-fault tenants get none.
coverage_conditions: Most Los Angeles residential rentals not regulated by the RSO, after six months in the unit or expiry of the original lease, whichever comes first; includes buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and a single-family dwelling.

applicability.other: tenant in the unit at least 6 months or original lease expired

exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner’s roommate, some cooperatives, some non-profit homeless or substance-abuse treatment facilities, and some HACLA or government-owned properties.
citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance: just cause eviction and relocation assistance
quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
interaction: JCO covers units not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance; RSO units are covered by the RSO instead.

title: California Tenant Protection Act AB 1482 annual rent cap
requirement: Annual rent increases on covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower; the allowable figure was 8.9% for August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025.
coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years on a rolling basis that are not already covered by the Los Angeles RSO or another listed exemption.

applicability.other: buildings older than 15 years, rolling basis

exemptions: Units constructed within the last 15 years, deed- or regulatory-restricted affordable units, certain dormitories, a two-unit property whose second unit was owner-occupied for the whole tenancy, some single-family homes and condominiums, and RSO units.
quoted_span:
Effective August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase is
8.9%
interaction: State law applies where the JCO does not regulate rent increases; units already under the City RSO are exempt from it.

title: LA non-payment eviction threshold, Fair Market Rent
requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes more than the Fair Market Rent for that bedroom size.
key_value: rent owed must exceed Fair Market Rent
coverage_conditions: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.
citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance: non-payment eviction, Fair Market Rent threshold
quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

title: LA eviction notices must be filed with LAHD
requirement: Every eviction notice served on a tenant in Los Angeles must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three business days of service.
coverage_conditions: All JCO and RSO rental properties in the City of Los Angeles.
citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance: eviction notice filing with LAHD
quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

title: RSO allowable rent increase, once every 12 months
requirement: Rent on a covered unit may be raised only once every 12 months and only by the City’s allowable rent increase percentage.
key_value: 1 increase per 12 months, by the allowable percentage
coverage_conditions: Rental properties in Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978 plus replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, including apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, ADUs and mobile homes.
exemptions: Rent is not regulated for condominium or townhome tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995; luxury exemption available on application.
citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance: allowable rent increase

title: RSO utility percentage increase prohibited
requirement: A landlord may no longer add an extra percentage rent increase for utilities on top of the allowable increase.
coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance: utility percentage increase prohibited
quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

title: RSO additional tenant and dependent increase
requirement: A 10% increase for an added dependent is no longer permitted; a 10% increase for an additional tenant is allowed within 60 days of learning of that tenant.
key_value: 10% for an additional tenant, within 60 days
coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance.

applicability.other: increase tied to an additional occupant, not a dependent

exemptions: No 10% increase is permitted for an additional dependent.
citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance: additional tenant increase
quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

title: RSO just cause eviction and relocation assistance
requirement: An RSO tenancy may be ended only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons; no-fault evictions require relocation assistance and 30- and 60-day written notice, some needing 120 days.
coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance: just cause eviction and relocation assistance
quoted_span:
No-fault evictions require the payment of
relocation assistance
.
Checklist for No-Fault Evictions
File a
Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict
filed with the LAHD.
Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).

title: RSO eviction notices filed with LAHD in three business days
requirement: All notices terminating an RSO tenancy must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three business days of service on the tenant.
coverage_conditions: All rental units subject to the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
quoted_span:
must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within
three (3) business days of service on the tenant
per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.
